attributeExplanations.criticalWarning: Active alert flags from the NVMe controller. Any non-zero value requires immediate investigation.
attributeExplanations.nvmeTemperature: Composite temperature reported by the controller. Sustained high temperatures cause thermal throttling and reduce NAND lifespan.
attributeExplanations.temperatureSensor1: Primary temperature sensor, usually the NAND flash. Most representative of flash health.
attributeExplanations.temperatureSensor2: Secondary sensor, often the controller die. Typically runs hotter than Sensor 1.
attributeExplanations.temperatureSensor3: Tertiary sensor, if present. Location varies by manufacturer.
attributeExplanations.availableSpare: Percentage of spare NAND blocks remaining for bad-block replacement. An alert triggers below the threshold.
attributeExplanations.availableSpareThreshold: Manufacturer-set minimum for Available Spare. Below this, the drive flags a critical warning.
attributeExplanations.percentageUsed: Drive estimate of endurance consumed based on actual versus rated write cycles. 100% means the rated TBW was reached; the drive may keep working beyond this.
attributeExplanations.mediaErrors: Unrecoverable read/write errors on NAND flash. Any non-zero value indicates permanent cell damage. Growing count means replace soon.
attributeExplanations.mediaIntegrityErrors: Unrecoverable errors detected by the controller. Non-zero means data corruption risk.
attributeExplanations.unsafeShutdowns: Power losses without proper flush or shutdown. Very high counts risk metadata corruption and firmware issues.
attributeExplanations.nvmePowerCycles: Total on/off cycles. Frequent cycling increases connector and capacitor wear.
attributeExplanations.nvmePowerOnHours: Total cumulative hours the drive has been powered on since manufacture.
attributeExplanations.dataUnitsRead: Total data read in 512 KB units. Multiply by 512,000 for bytes. Useful for calculating daily read workload.
attributeExplanations.dataUnitsWritten: Total data written in 512 KB units. Compare with TBW rating to estimate remaining endurance.
attributeExplanations.hostReadCommands: Total read commands issued by the host. A high ratio versus write commands indicates a read-heavy workload.
attributeExplanations.hostWriteCommands: Total write commands issued by the host. Includes filesystem metadata writes.
attributeExplanations.controllerBusyTime: Total minutes the controller spent processing I/O commands. High values indicate sustained heavy workload.
attributeExplanations.errorLogEntries: Number of entries in the error information log. Often includes benign self-test artifacts; cross-check with Media Errors.
attributeExplanations.warningTempTime: Total minutes spent above the warning temperature threshold. Causes performance throttling. Zero is ideal.
attributeExplanations.criticalTempTime: Total minutes spent above the critical temperature threshold. The drive may shut down to prevent damage. Should always be zero.
attributeExplanations.warningCompositeTemperatureTime: Total minutes the composite temperature exceeded the warning threshold.
attributeExplanations.criticalCompositeTemperatureTime: Total minutes the composite temperature exceeded the critical threshold. Must be zero.
attributeExplanations.thermalManagementT1TransCount: Number of times the drive entered light thermal throttling (T1). Indicates cooling issues.
attributeExplanations.thermalManagementT2TransCount: Number of times the drive entered heavy thermal throttling (T2). Significant performance impact.
attributeExplanations.thermalManagementT1TotalTime: Total seconds spent in light thermal throttling. Indicates sustained cooling problems.
attributeExplanations.thermalManagementT2TotalTime: Total seconds spent in heavy thermal throttling. Severe performance degradation.
attributeExplanations.rawReadErrorRate: Hardware read errors detected. High raw values on Seagate/Samsung drives are normal because their proprietary formula makes VALUE more important than raw.
attributeExplanations.writeErrorRate: Errors encountered during write operations. A growing count may indicate head or media issues.
attributeExplanations.multiZoneErrorRate: Errors when writing to multi-zone regions. Manufacturer-specific; a rising trend is concerning.
attributeExplanations.softReadErrorRate: Read errors corrected by firmware without data loss. High values may indicate degrading media.
attributeExplanations.readErrorRetryRate: Number of read retries needed. Occasional retries are normal; persistent growth indicates wear.
attributeExplanations.reportedUncorrect: Errors that ECC could not correct. Any non-zero value means data was lost or unreadable.
attributeExplanations.reportedUncorrectableErrors: Errors that ECC could not correct. Non-zero means data loss risk.
attributeExplanations.reallocatedSectorCount: Bad sectors replaced by spare sectors from the reserve pool. A growing count means drive degradation.
attributeExplanations.retiredBlockCount: NAND blocks retired due to wear or failure (SSD). Similar to Reallocated Sector Count for HDDs.
attributeExplanations.reallocatedEventCount: Number of remap operations performed. Each event means a bad sector was replaced.
attributeExplanations.currentPendingSector: Unstable sectors waiting to be remapped on next write. They may resolve or become permanently reallocated.
attributeExplanations.pendingSectors: Sectors waiting to be remapped. They may resolve or become reallocated.
attributeExplanations.offlineUncorrectable: Sectors that failed during offline scan and could not be corrected. Indicates possible data loss.
attributeExplanations.offlineUncorrectableSectorCount: Uncorrectable sectors found during background scan. Data on these sectors is lost.
attributeExplanations.sataTemperature: Current drive temperature. Sustained high temperatures accelerate wear and reduce lifespan.
attributeExplanations.temperatureCelsius: Current drive temperature in Celsius. HDDs should usually stay below 45°C; SSDs below 60°C.
attributeExplanations.airflowTemperatureCel: Temperature measured by the airflow sensor. Usually slightly lower than the main temperature sensor.
attributeExplanations.temperatureCase: Temperature of the drive casing. Useful for monitoring enclosure ventilation.
attributeExplanations.temperatureInternal: Internal temperature sensor. May read higher than case temperature.
attributeExplanations.sataPowerOnHours: Total cumulative hours the drive has been powered on. Used to estimate age and plan replacements.
attributeExplanations.powerOnHoursAndMsec: Total powered-on time with millisecond precision.
attributeExplanations.powerCycleCount: Total number of complete power on/off cycles. Frequent cycling stresses electronics.
attributeExplanations.powerOffRetractCount: Times the heads were retracted due to power loss (HDD). High values indicate unstable power supply.
attributeExplanations.unexpectedPowerLossCt: Unexpected power losses (SSD). Can cause metadata corruption if write cache was active.
attributeExplanations.unsafeShutdownCount: Power losses without proper shutdown (SSD). High values risk firmware corruption.
attributeExplanations.startStopCount: Spindle motor start/stop cycles (HDD). Each cycle causes mechanical wear.
attributeExplanations.spinUpTime: Time for platters to reach full operating speed (HDD). Increasing values may indicate motor bearing wear.
attributeExplanations.spinRetryCount: Failed attempts to spin up the motor (HDD). Non-zero usually indicates power supply or motor issues.
attributeExplanations.calibrationRetryCount: Number of head calibration retries (HDD). Non-zero may indicate mechanical issues.
attributeExplanations.seekErrorRate: Errors during head positioning (HDD). High raw values on Seagate are often normal due to a proprietary formula.
attributeExplanations.seekTimePerformance: Average seek operation performance (HDD). Declining values suggest mechanical degradation.
attributeExplanations.loadCycleCount: Head load/unload cycles (HDD). Rated for 300K-600K cycles on most drives.
attributeExplanations.loadUnloadCycleCount: Head load/unload cycles (HDD). Each cycle causes small wear on the ramp mechanism.
attributeExplanations.headFlyingHours: Hours the read/write heads have been positioned over the platters (HDD).
attributeExplanations.highFlyWrites: Writes where the head flew higher than expected (HDD). Data may not be written correctly.
attributeExplanations.gSenseErrorRate: Shock or vibration events detected by the accelerometer (HDD). High values indicate physical disturbance.
attributeExplanations.diskShift: Distance the disk has shifted from its original position (HDD). Temperature or shock related.
attributeExplanations.loadedHours: Hours spent with heads loaded over the platters (HDD).
attributeExplanations.loadInTime: Time of the head loading process. Manufacturer-specific diagnostic metric.
attributeExplanations.torqueAmplificationCount: Times the drive needed extra torque to spin up. May indicate stiction or motor issues.
attributeExplanations.flyingHeight: Head-to-platter distance during operation (HDD). Critical for read/write reliability.
attributeExplanations.loadFriction: Friction detected during head loading (HDD). Increasing values suggest ramp mechanism wear.
attributeExplanations.loadUnloadRetryCount: Failed head load/unload attempts (HDD). Non-zero indicates mechanical issues.
attributeExplanations.udmaCrcErrorCount: Data transfer checksum errors on the SATA cable. Usually caused by a bad cable, loose connection, or port issue.
attributeExplanations.crcErrors: Interface communication errors. Usually caused by cable or connection issues.
attributeExplanations.crcErrorCount: Data transfer checksum errors. Replace the SATA cable if this value grows.
attributeExplanations.commandTimeout: Commands that took too long and timed out. May indicate controller or connection issues.
attributeExplanations.interfaceCrcErrorCount: CRC errors on the interface link. Cable or connector problem.
attributeExplanations.hardwareEccRecovered: Read errors corrected by hardware ECC. Non-zero is normal; rapid growth warrants attention.
attributeExplanations.eccErrorRate: Rate of ECC-corrected errors. Proprietary formula; VALUE matters more than raw count.
attributeExplanations.endToEndError: Data corruption detected between the controller cache and host interface. Should always be zero.
attributeExplanations.endToEndErrorDetectionCount: Number of parity errors in the data path. Non-zero indicates controller issues.
attributeExplanations.wearLevelingCount: Average erase cycles per NAND block (SSD). Lower VALUE means more wear consumed.
attributeExplanations.wearRangeDelta: Difference between most-worn and least-worn blocks (SSD). High values indicate uneven wear.
attributeExplanations.mediaWearoutIndicator: Intel SSD life remaining estimate. Starts at 100 and decreases to 0 as endurance is consumed.
attributeExplanations.ssdLifeLeft: Estimated remaining SSD lifespan percentage based on NAND wear.
attributeExplanations.percentLifetimeRemain: Estimated remaining lifespan percentage. 100 means new; 0 means end of rated life.
attributeExplanations.percentLifetimeUsed: Percentage of rated endurance consumed. Inverse of Percent Lifetime Remain.
attributeExplanations.availableReservedSpace: Remaining spare blocks as a percentage (SSD). Low values reduce the drive's ability to handle bad blocks.
attributeExplanations.usedReservedBlockCount: Reserve blocks consumed for bad-block replacement (SSD). A growing value means aging.
attributeExplanations.unusedReservedBlockCount: Reserve blocks still available for bad-block replacement (SSD). Zero means no more bad-block replacement is possible.
attributeExplanations.programFailCount: NAND write failures (SSD). A growing count means flash cells are wearing out.
attributeExplanations.programFailCountChip: Program failures at chip level (SSD). Non-zero indicates NAND degradation.
attributeExplanations.eraseFailCount: NAND erase operation failures (SSD). Non-zero indicates severe flash wear.
attributeExplanations.eraseFailCountTotal: Total NAND erase failures (SSD). Combined with Program Fail Count, it shows overall NAND health.
attributeExplanations.eraseFailCountChip: Erase failures at chip level (SSD). Non-zero means NAND degradation.
attributeExplanations.runtimeBadBlock: Bad blocks discovered during normal operation (SSD). A growing count means flash is wearing out.
attributeExplanations.totalLbasWritten: Total logical block addresses written. Multiply by 512 bytes for total data volume.
attributeExplanations.totalLbasRead: Total logical block addresses read. Useful for calculating daily workload.
attributeExplanations.lifetimeWritesGib: Total data written in GiB over the drive's lifetime.
attributeExplanations.lifetimeReadsGib: Total data read in GiB over the drive's lifetime.
attributeExplanations.totalWritesGib: Total data written in GiB. Compare with TBW rating for endurance estimate.
attributeExplanations.nandWritesGib: Raw NAND writes in GiB. Higher than host writes due to write amplification.
attributeExplanations.hostWrites32Mib: Total data written by the host in 32 MiB units.
attributeExplanations.hostReads32Mib: Total data read by the host in 32 MiB units.
attributeExplanations.hostWritesMib: Total data written by the host in MiB.
attributeExplanations.hostReadsMib: Total data read by the host in MiB.
attributeExplanations.nandGbWrittenTlc: Total data written to TLC NAND cells in GB. Includes write amplification overhead.
attributeExplanations.nandGibWritten: Total NAND writes in GiB. Higher than host writes due to write amplification and garbage collection.
attributeExplanations.averageBlockEraseCount: Average number of erase cycles per NAND block (SSD). Drives are typically rated for 3K-100K cycles.
attributeExplanations.averageEraseCount: Average erase cycles per block. Compare with rated endurance for remaining life estimate.
attributeExplanations.maxEraseCount: Maximum erase cycles on any single block. A large gap with average indicates uneven wear.
attributeExplanations.totalEraseCount: Sum of all erase cycles across all blocks. Overall NAND write volume indicator.
attributeExplanations.powerLossCapTest: Result of the power-loss protection capacitor self-test (SSD). Failed means risk of data loss on power failure.
attributeExplanations.powerLossProtection: Status of the power-loss protection mechanism. Enterprise SSDs use capacitors to flush cache on power loss.
attributeExplanations.successfulRainRecovCnt: Successful recoveries using RAIN (Redundant Array of Independent NAND). Shows NAND parity is working.
attributeExplanations.ssdEraseFailCount: Total erase failures across the SSD. Indicates overall NAND degradation.
attributeExplanations.ssdProgramFailCount: Total write failures across the SSD. Indicates flash cell reliability issues.
attributeExplanations.throughputPerformance: Overall throughput performance rating (HDD). Declining values indicate degradation.
attributeExplanations.unknownAttribute: Vendor-specific attribute not defined in the SMART standard. Check manufacturer documentation.
attributeExplanations.freeFallSensor: Free-fall events detected (laptop HDD). The heads are parked to prevent damage during drops.
attributeExplanations.grownDefectList: Sectors remapped due to defects found during operation. Equivalent to Reallocated Sectors on SATA. A growing count means drive degradation.
attributeExplanations.readErrorsCorrected: Read errors corrected by ECC. Normal for enterprise drives under heavy workload; only uncorrected errors are critical.
attributeExplanations.readEccFast: Errors corrected by fast on-the-fly ECC during read operations. Normal in SAS drives.
attributeExplanations.readEccDelayed: Errors requiring delayed or offline ECC correction during reads. Non-zero is acceptable but should not grow rapidly.
attributeExplanations.readUncorrectedErrors: Read errors that ECC could not correct. Non-zero means data was lost or unreadable. Critical metric.
attributeExplanations.readDataProcessed: Total data read by the drive. Useful for calculating daily workload.
attributeExplanations.writeErrorsCorrected: Write errors corrected by ECC. Normal for enterprise drives.
attributeExplanations.writeUncorrectedErrors: Write errors that ECC could not correct. Non-zero means potential data loss. Critical.
attributeExplanations.writeDataProcessed: Total data written to the drive. Useful for workload analysis.
attributeExplanations.verifyErrorsCorrected: Verification errors corrected during background verify operations.
attributeExplanations.verifyUncorrectedErrors: Verify errors that could not be corrected. Non-zero indicates media degradation.
attributeExplanations.nonMediumErrors: Controller or bus errors not related to the media itself. High count may indicate backplane or cable issues.
attributeExplanations.sasTemperature: Current drive temperature. Enterprise SAS drives tolerate up to 55-60°C under sustained load.
attributeExplanations.sasPowerOnHours: Total hours the drive has been powered on. Enterprise drives are rated for 24/7 operation.
attributeExplanations.startStopCycles: Motor start/stop cycles. Enterprise SAS drives are rated for 50,000+ cycles.
attributeExplanations.loadUnloadCycles: Head load/unload cycles. Enterprise drives are rated for 600,000+ cycles.
attributeExplanations.backgroundScanStatus: Status of the SCSI background media scan. Runs continuously to detect surface defects.

recommendations.healthyText: All SMART attributes are within normal ranges. Continue regular monitoring.
recommendations.criticalText: SMART has reported a health issue. Back up all data immediately and plan for disk replacement.
recommendations.reallocatedText: The disk has bad sectors that have been remapped. Monitor it closely and consider replacement if the count increases.
recommendations.pendingText: Some sectors are waiting to be reallocated. This may indicate an impending failure.
recommendations.hotHdd: The HDD is running hot. Improve case airflow or add cooling.
recommendations.hotSsd: The SSD is running hot. Check airflow around the drive.
recommendations.hotNvme: The NVMe is overheating. Consider adding a heatsink or improving case airflow.
recommendations.maintenanceText: Schedule an extended SMART test every month to catch issues early.
recommendations.backupText: Back up critical data regularly, regardless of disk health.
recommendations.nvmeWarningText: The NVMe controller has raised an alert. Back up data immediately and investigate further.
recommendations.nvmeMediaText: Unrecoverable NAND flash errors indicate physical damage. Back up data and plan for replacement.
recommendations.unsafeText: Frequent power losses increase the risk of firmware corruption. Ensure stable power or use a UPS.
recommendations.seagateText: Seagate drives report very large raw values for attribute #1. This is expected; only the normalized value matters and it should remain at 100.
recommendations.smrText: SMR disks write random data more slowly and may stall under a heavy mixed workload. They suit backups and archives, but are not recommended as primary Proxmox storage or ZFS vdevs.

currentFeatures.appDetection: Smarter app detection in the App tab: Docker is correctly promoted as the parent workload during cold start (Portainer/SearXNG no longer briefly show up as native apps), unregistered suggestions live in the startup cache, and 'Find applications' runs a fresh catalog-backed scan on demand.
currentFeatures.dockerUpdates: The Updates tab now covers Docker end-to-end: Docker Engine and per-image update tracking follow the same 24-hour rolling cycle as OS packages, with a 'Check now' action for on-demand digest comparison — no more waiting for the daily collector.
currentFeatures.appCatalog: New application detection catalog with over 380 tracked workloads, generated live from community-scripts across seven detector methods (file, binary, dpkg, apk, Python, Docker exec, Docker label). Primary and fallback detectors cover both new and historical LXC layouts.
currentFeatures.pushover: Pushover joins Telegram, Gotify, Discord, Email and Apprise as a native notification channel — user/API key, device and sound selectors, priority 0 for regular messages, optional priority 1 for CRITICAL events. Suggested by @benginx (#308).
currentFeatures.appsDashboard: New top-level Apps dashboard — a single launcher for every Web Link across the node. LXC-registered apps and user-defined Custom Web Links share the same grid with category badges, search, and one-click deep-links back to the guest modal.
currentFeatures.lxcAppsUpdates: App tab inside every LXC modal registers installed apps, captures weblinks and tracks upstream versions. Reworked Updates tab applies OS packages and app updates from a single button; Docker Engine and per-image tracking follow the same 24-hour cycle, with a 'Check now' action on demand.
currentFeatures.multilingual: The Monitor now speaks 8 languages: English, Spanish, German, French, Italian, Portuguese, Swedish and Slovak. Huge thanks to @vaso73 for building the i18n scaffolding that made this possible.
currentFeatures.nvidiaMultiGpu: NVIDIA driver lifecycle moves to per-BDF ownership so a multi-GPU host can pass one card to a VM and keep the other operational on the host or in LXCs, plus a kernel + branch + GPU-aware version picker (#298).
